industry-4-0.title: Manufacturing Industry 4.0 Technologies – Microsoft
industry-4-0.notes: Industry 4.0 describes the use of advanced technologies such as IoT, AI, cloud computing and data analytics in manufacturing; the page also calls it the fourth industrial revolution or Manufacturing 4.0. It places the idea after mechanization, mass production and the computer era. The goals are more automation, predictive maintenance and processes that optimize themselves, which the page links to productivity, asset utilization, quality and leaner logistics. Core building blocks listed are cloud computing, IoT sensors on machines and products, digital twins, big data and analytics, edge computing close to the data source, AI and machine learning, and cybersecurity. The page stresses that the full potential appears only when these technologies work together. Before starting, organizations should assess their digital maturity and how new technology fits existing systems. Challenges named include integrating legacy equipment, skill gaps in data science, AI and security, a larger attack surface from connectivity, and heavy demands on storage and compute.

az-900.title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals – Microsoft Learn
az-900.notes: Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals is a beginner-level certification earned by passing exam AZ-900. It demonstrates foundational knowledge of cloud concepts in general and of Microsoft Azure in particular, and the page describes it as a common starting point for a career in the Azure space. The exam covers three areas: describing cloud concepts, describing Azure architecture and services such as compute, networking and storage, and describing Azure management and governance, including security, governance and administration tools. No formal prerequisite is listed, though experience in an IT area such as infrastructure, database administration or software development is recommended. The exam is proctored, offered in many languages and booked through Pearson VUE, or through Certiport for students and educators. Preparation options include a practice assessment, an exam sandbox and a study guide. The page does not give a passing score, question count or renewal rules.

adaptive-card-extensions.title: Overview of Viva Connections Extensibility – Microsoft Learn
adaptive-card-extensions.notes: Adaptive Card Extensions, or ACEs, are described as the foundation of the personalization and extensibility model in Viva Connections. They are built with the SharePoint Framework as client-side extensions, and the page states that all customization and extension work for Viva Connections relies on that framework. Their purpose is to shape the Viva Connections dashboard around organizational needs by adding new cards and experiences that surface the information and apps relevant to a person's role. Dashboards can be personalized or set up separately for different audiences. ACEs appear in the desktop experience through the Microsoft Teams client, on tablets and in the Teams mobile app, where the mobile view shows the same ACEs as the desktop by default, adapted for mobile. The page only names Card View and Quick View as topics of further articles and does not explain them itself. It does not state licensing requirements or technical limits.

adaptive-scopes.title: Adaptive scopes – Microsoft Purview – Microsoft Learn
adaptive-scopes.notes: An adaptive scope in Microsoft Purview is a query-based scope whose membership is determined dynamically from attributes or properties, such as Microsoft Entra attributes, instead of a manually maintained list. It lets administrators target policies for communication compliance, retention and auto-labeling at users, SharePoint sites or Microsoft 365 groups. Queries can be built with a simple query builder or an advanced builder that uses OPATH syntax for users and groups and KeyQL for sites. The query is evaluated once a day, so changes are not validated immediately and can take several days to take effect. One scope can be assigned to several policies, and one policy can contain several scopes. A typical example is limiting a policy to people in a particular country or department. Administrators need the Scope Manager role, and the page refers to the Purview service description for licensing. It lists limits for query length, attribute counts and group counts.

advanced-specialization.title: Apply for specializations – Partner Center – Microsoft Learn
advanced-specialization.notes: Specializations are credentials within the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program that show deeper expertise in a specific area, grouped under Azure, Modern Work, Security and Business Applications. A partner generally needs an active Solutions Partner designation in a matching solution area, plus the specific requirements of the chosen specialization. Those requirements combine performance criteria, such as consumed Azure revenue or unique customers, skilling criteria based on individual certifications, and sometimes a marketplace offer. Proof of capability is delivered either through an audit by a third-party auditor or through customer references drawn from separate recent customer projects, depending on the specialization. Only users with the partner admin role see the Specializations area in Partner Center, where progress is tracked and audits are scheduled. A failed audit can be repeated after a waiting period, and some retired specializations accept no new applications. Trial, benefit, support and internal consumption does not count toward revenue requirements.

agent-card.title: A2A Hosting – Microsoft Agent Framework – Microsoft Learn
agent-card.notes: An agent card describes an agent in the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol through metadata such as its name, description, version and the interfaces it supports. Its purpose is discovery: a client can learn what an agent offers before sending any request. In the ASP.NET Core hosting example, the card is served at a well-known path ending in agent-card.json, using a mapping method that comes from the A2A SDK package rather than from the Agent Framework hosting packages. The sample card sets name, description, version, default input and output modes, and a supported interface with a URL, a protocol binding and a protocol version. The page recommends a fully populated card for production use. A limitation is that a single host can publish only one agent card at the well-known path, so only one agent is discoverable there. Other agents stay reachable by their own URLs, and clients must know those endpoints. The page does not cover skills, authentication or card signatures.

ai-evaluation.title: Observability in Generative AI – Microsoft Foundry – Microsoft Learn
ai-evaluation.notes: In Microsoft Foundry, evaluation measures the quality, safety and reliability of model and agent outputs, both during development and in production, and forms one part of observability alongside tracing and monitoring. Evaluators are the scoring methods: some compute results deterministically, while AI-assisted ones use a judge model that rates responses and can explain its rating. Built-in evaluators cover general quality such as coherence and fluency, retrieval scenarios such as groundedness and relevance, safety categories, and agent behavior such as tool call accuracy and task completion. Teams can also write custom evaluators for domain needs. Data can come from existing datasets, generated responses, production traces or simulated conversations. An AI red teaming agent can probe a system with simulated attacks and is best used with a human in the loop. Evaluation is applied at model selection, before deployment and continuously afterward, with alerts when thresholds are breached. AI-assisted evaluators depend on a judge model and on regional availability and rate limits.

altair-8800.title: The History of Microsoft – 1975 – Microsoft Learn
altair-8800.notes: The MITS Altair 8800 was a personal computer made by MITS, a company in Albuquerque, New Mexico. It appeared on the cover of Popular Electronics at the start of 1975, and that article inspired Paul Allen and Bill Gates to write a BASIC language for it. The page does not describe the hardware or its specifications. Gates and Allen finished Altair BASIC and sold it to MITS, and MITS became Microsoft's first customer. Paul Allen joined MITS as director of software, and a licensing agreement for the BASIC interpreter was signed between Allen, Gates and MITS later that year. The page calls Altair BASIC the first computer language program for a personal computer. Version 2.0 shipped in 4K and 8K editions, and the first edition of MITS Computer Notes ran the headline Altair BASIC Up and Running.

application-security-groups.title: Azure Application Security Groups overview – Microsoft Learn
application-security-groups.notes: Application security groups are a feature of Azure Virtual Network that lets you group virtual machine network interfaces and write network security policy based on those groups. Instead of maintaining explicit IP addresses, you use a group as the source or destination in a network security group rule, and the platform handles the underlying addresses and rule sets. A network interface can belong to several groups. A rule applies only to interfaces that are members of the referenced group, so an interface without membership is not affected even when the network security group is attached to its subnet. The page illustrates a three-tier layout with web, logic and database groups, where one rule allows internet traffic to the web group and another lets only the logic group reach the database port, followed by a deny rule for everyone else. All interfaces in a group must be in the same virtual network as the first interface assigned. The page recommends service tags or application security groups over raw IP ranges to reduce the number of rules.

atea.title: Atea drives B2B innovation with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Microsoft Customer Stories
atea.notes: Atea is described in this Microsoft customer story as a provider of IT infrastructure that serves organizations in the Nordic and Baltic regions. The page gives its footprint as offices in 85 cities and more than 7,500 employees. Its portfolio covers Digital Workplace, Hybrid Platforms and Information Management, supported by lifecycle, professional and managed services. Much of its B2B business runs through an online store called eShop, which handles most of its orders. The story explains how Atea chose Dynamics 365 Customer Insights as a customer data platform alongside Dynamics 365 Marketing and Power BI. It unified data from Dataverse contacts and accounts, eShop users and transactions, and a custom AI product recommendation model into customer profiles. Segments of new, existing and at-risk customers were sent to Dynamics 365 Marketing for automated welcome, retention and win-back campaigns, with exclusion rules for customers who had not given marketing consent. The page does not state the location of the company's headquarters.

attack-simulation-training.title: Get started using Attack simulation training – Microsoft Defender for Office 365 – Microsoft Learn
attack-simulation-training.notes: Attack simulation training is a feature of Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, found in the Microsoft Defender portal. It runs realistic but harmless phishing simulations so that vulnerable users can be identified before a real attack, and it can also assign training without a simulation. A simulation combines recipients, a schedule, a payload such as a link or attachment, and a social engineering technique, most of which follow the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Automations can combine several techniques and payloads, and payload automation can harvest harmless versions of real phishing messages seen in Microsoft 365. Training campaigns, how-to guides, landing pages and notifications round out the feature, and reports show who deleted, reported, clicked or entered credentials. A predicted compromise rate estimates how many users might fall for a payload. Licensing requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, and administration uses Entra roles such as Attack Simulation Administrator. Reporting is limited for on-premises mailboxes, and some functions are missing in GCC High and DoD.

auto-capture.title: Auto capture customer-related activities – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
auto-capture.notes: Auto capture in Dynamics 365 Sales simplifies logging of customer-related activities by generating activity suggestions for emails and meetings based on data from the user's Outlook account. Relevant items show up on the timeline of a record alongside other activities, so sellers spend less time on manual entry. Suggestions can be saved or deleted, and they are private to the individual user at first. Once an email or meeting is tracked, it becomes visible to anyone with access to the related record. Supported timeline records include contacts, opportunities, leads, accounts, cases and custom entities. An administrator must enable the feature before users can work with it, and the setup is covered in a separate article. The page does not list licensing requirements, mailbox types, regional restrictions or technical limits.

availability-sets.title: Availability sets overview – Azure Virtual Machines – Microsoft Learn
availability-sets.notes: An availability set is a logical grouping of virtual machines that lowers the chance of a correlated failure affecting all related machines at once. It spreads machines across fault domains, which share a power source and network switch, and update domains, which are groups that can be restarted together during planned maintenance. Only one update domain is restarted at a time, with a recovery pause before the next one. The number of fault and update domains cannot be changed after creation. For the platform's availability SLA, a set needs at least two virtual machines, and a managed set accepts only machines with managed disks. There is no extra charge beyond the machines themselves, and latency between machines can be lower than with availability zones. Availability sets do not protect against operating system or application faults, remain exposed to some shared infrastructure outages, and give less resilience than availability zones. For new designs the page points to scale sets in flexible orchestration mode.

azure-ai-content-understanding.title: What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools? – Microsoft Learn
azure-ai-content-understanding.notes: Azure Content Understanding is a Foundry tool that uses generative AI to turn unstructured content into structured output for automation and analytics workflows. It handles documents, images, video and audio. Processing is driven by an analyzer, which defines extraction settings, the field schema and the model deployments; prebuilt analyzers cover common scenarios and custom analyzers cover specific ones. The pipeline includes content extraction such as OCR, layout and transcription, optional segmentation, and field extraction that can extract, classify or generate values. Confidence scores and grounding to source regions are available for document analyzers. Results come back as Markdown for search and retrieval scenarios or as JSON that follows the schema. Typical uses include document processing, agent inputs, search indexing, process automation and routing documents by class. It requires a Foundry resource and deployments of supported models. Content safety guardrails can restrict extraction, so warnings should be checked, and some features exist only in the preview API version.

azure-api-center.title: Azure API Center – Overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-api-center.notes: Azure API Center is a service that lets an organization register all of its APIs in one central inventory, including versions, definition files and shared metadata, regardless of type, lifecycle stage or where the API is deployed. Its aim is discovery, reuse and governance. The page positions it as design-time governance and discovery, while Azure API Management covers runtime governance through a gateway. APIs can be added from API Management, other platforms, unmanaged sources and APIs still in development, using the Azure portal, the Azure CLI or pipelines. Governance features include built-in and custom metadata plus linting and analysis of definitions such as OpenAPI to enforce quality standards. A Visual Studio Code extension offers linting, breaking-change detection and GitHub Copilot integration, and a portal supports discovery. Integration with Dev Proxy can reveal unregistered shadow APIs. A free plan suits evaluation and has no Microsoft support, while a standard plan targets production. The service is not a runtime gateway and is offered only in listed regions.

azure-compute-gallery.title: Overview of Azure Compute Gallery – Azure Virtual Machines – Microsoft Learn
azure-compute-gallery.notes: Azure Compute Gallery gives structure and organization to resources such as virtual machine images and VM applications. It offers global replication, versioning and grouping, zone-redundant storage in regions with availability zones, and sharing with subscriptions, tenants or a community. The building blocks are the gallery itself, image definitions that group images, and image versions that are replicated to target regions. VM applications are separate resources, so changing an application does not require a new image. The service is not a global resource, so the page advises keeping galleries in separate regions for disaster recovery. Sharing is recommended at gallery level rather than for single image versions. Replica counts can be scaled for large parallel deployments, and replicating only the newest version widely can save cost. The page lists per-subscription limits for galleries, definitions, versions and replicas, and notes that moving gallery resources is not supported. The gallery itself is free, while storage per replica and network egress are billed.

azure-dedicated-host.title: Azure Dedicated Host – Azure Virtual Machines – Microsoft Learn
azure-dedicated-host.notes: Azure Dedicated Host provides physical servers that run virtual machines belonging to a single Azure subscription. These are the same servers used in Azure datacenters, exposed as a hardware resource and placed by region, availability zone and fault domain. The benefits named are hardware isolation at server level, control over platform maintenance timing, choice over which workloads share physical resources, and the option to bring Windows and SQL licenses through Azure Hybrid Benefit. A host group is a collection of hosts tied to one zone, and a host is a single physical server with a SKU that decides which VM sizes it can run. Only machines from the same family as the host can be placed on it. A host's size and type cannot be changed after deployment, and live migration is not supported, so a hardware failure leads to service healing with brief unavailability. Billing is per host rather than per VM, and licenses, storage and networking are charged separately. Deployment needs dedicated host quota and matching VM family quota.
